definitions.gloss: sensitivity to cold; poor circulation; tendency to feel cold
definitions.explanation: A constitutional tendency to feel cold easily, especially in the hands, feet, and lower body. Recognized in Japanese and East Asian medicine as a condition requiring treatment. Much more commonly discussed in Japan than in Western cultures.

examples.japanese: ⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{冷|ひ}え{性|しょう}で、⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧つらい。
examples.english: I'm sensitive to cold, so winter is tough for me.

examples.japanese: {冷|ひ}え{性|しょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{改善|かいぜん}する→改善する：26828_kaizensuru⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{生姜|しょうが}→生姜：05191_shouga⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧ようにして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: I try to eat ginger to improve my cold sensitivity.

examples.japanese: ⟦{女性|じょせい}→女性：01617_josei⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{男性|だんせい}→男性：01655_dansei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{比|くら}べて→比べる：01237_kuraberu⟧{冷|ひ}え{性|しょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なり→なる：01970_naru⟧やすい⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: Women are said to be more prone to cold sensitivity than men.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
A concept deeply rooted in East Asian medicine. In Japan, {冷|ひ}え{性|しょう} is widely recognized as a legitimate health concern, and many remedies are marketed for it — from warming foods like ginger to hot baths and special socks. The concept has no direct equivalent in Western medicine.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {冷|ひ}え{性|しょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{改善|かいぜん}する→改善する：26828_kaizensuru⟧ (to improve cold sensitivity)
- {冷|ひ}え{性|しょう}⟦{対策|たいさく}→対策：02511_taisaku⟧ (measures against cold sensitivity)
- ⟦{末端|まったん}→末端：06788_mattan⟧{冷|ひ}え{性|しょう} (cold extremities — cold hands and feet)
- {冷|ひ}え{性|しょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{効|き}く→効く：01932_kiku⟧ (effective for cold sensitivity)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {寒|さむ}⟦がり→ガリ：27408_gari⟧: person who feels the cold — describes a person's temperament rather than a medical condition
